verification_report.summary: The proof is correct. The sequential audit verifies both assertions and the stated consequence. Near the good-reduction point, normalized analytic moment coordinates agree in absolute value with constant rational lifts of their reductions, so every ordinary smooth weight has a finite real-principal outgoing-slope divisor of degree zero. The residual-disc test function is ordinary smooth and compactly supported. Its radial integration has multiplicity one, and integration by parts gives the limit d_R-a_R, with the remainder tending to zero. Thus a_R<=d_R. Degree zero forces equality, and rational linear algebra followed by clearing denominators makes the divisor class torsion. The converse construction also gives a smooth pluriharmonic metric. The transcendental coordinate makes P non-torsion, so this obstruction excludes every global ordinary smooth psh metric on L. The displayed weights are those of the continuous constant-model metric, whose degree on its only special-fiber component is zero, proving nefness. The elliptic group law gives the stated principal divisor for f_n. The convex cutoff exists, agrees with the logarithmic formula on an outer collar, extends constantly over the disc center, and has nonnegative smooth Hessian. Its error is bounded by max{a,2}/n on the same neighborhood V for every n. The cited CLD dependencies and their hypotheses were checked in the [25 July 2025 primary source](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~antoine.chambert-loir/publications/papers/fdceb-20250725.pdf). Definition 8.1.7 uses sheaf closure under uniform limits; the proof needs only this valid sufficient direction. Definitions 17.8.1 and 17.8.5 distinguish local psh weights from global uniform approximation exactly as required. Frame changes preserve local psh, while the absence of any global smooth psh metric excludes global approximation. No critical errors or gaps remain.
